# Birko.Data.EventSourcing

<!-- spec-links: generated by Birko.Framework/spec-links.cs from docs/specs/.map.yml. Do not edit: change the map and run `dotnet run spec-links.cs`. -->
**Specs**: [store-decorator-composition](../Birko.Framework/docs/specs/store-decorator-composition.md)

## Overview
Decorator-style event sourcing for Birko stores. Wraps any `IStore<T>` / `IAsyncStore<T>` (incl. bulk variants) so every Create / Update / Delete also appends a `DomainEvent` to an `IEventStore`. Reads pass through to the inner store. Provides Replay + history APIs to rebuild aggregate state from the event stream.

This project ships **interfaces, wrappers, and an aggregate base class only** — no snapshot store, no built-in projections. The one shipped backend is the sibling **Birko.Data.EventSourcing.SQL** (`SqlEventStore<DB>`, async, any SQL provider — TASK-529); anything else, bring your own.

## Project Location
`Birko.Data.EventSourcing/`

## Layout

```
Events/
  IEvent.cs                — domain event contract
  DomainEvent.cs           — default IEvent implementation
  IEventStore.cs           — IEventStore + IAsyncEventStore (append + read by aggregate/version/time)
Models/
  IEventSourced.cs         — IEventSourced contract + EventSourcedAggregate base class
  EventRecord.cs           — one stored event for the generic event store; id = name-based UUID of (aggregate, version)
Stores/
  AbstractAsyncEventStore.cs     — base of every IAsyncEventStore: non-virtual contract, *Core seams (TASK-995)
  AsyncStoreEventStore.cs        — the default event store over any IAsyncBulkStore<EventRecord>
  EventStoreFactoryExtensions.cs — factory.GetEventStore(o => …) + EventStoreOverrides
  EventSourcingStoreWrapper.cs           — sync IStore<T> wrapper
  AsyncEventSourcingStoreWrapper.cs      — async IAsyncStore<T> wrapper
  EventSourcingBulkStoreWrapper.cs       — sync IBulkStore<T> wrapper (extends sync wrapper)
  AsyncEventSourcingBulkStoreWrapper.cs  — async IAsyncBulkStore<T> wrapper
  EventSourcingStoreExtensions.cs        — .WithEventSourcing(...) extension methods
  EventSourcingRepositoryExtensions.cs   — EXCLUDED from compilation (depends on Birko.Data.ViewModel);
                                           consumers needing event-sourced ViewModel repos include it explicitly
```

## Components

### `IEvent` / `DomainEvent` (`Events/`)
`IEvent` fields: `EventGuid`, `AggregateGuid`, `Version`, `EventType` (string — `"Created"` / `"Updated"` / `"Deleted"` by default), `OccurredAt`, `EventData` (serialized entity, JSON), `Metadata?`, `UserGuid?`.

`DomainEvent` is the default `IEvent` implementation. Two constructors: parameterless (auto-assigns `EventGuid` + `OccurredAt`) and a fully-specified one used by the wrappers.

### `IEventStore` / `IAsyncEventStore` (`Events/IEventStore.cs`)
The event-store contract consumed by the wrappers. Members:
- `Append(IEvent)` / `AppendRange(IEnumerable<IEvent>)`
- `Read(Guid aggregateId)` — all events for an aggregate, in order
- `ReadUpToVersion(Guid, long)` / `ReadFromVersion(Guid, long)` — version-range slices
- `GetVersion(Guid)` — current aggregate version (0 if none)
- `ReadAllFrom(DateTime)` — global tail-read by time

Async variants take a `CancellationToken`.

### The event stores (TASK-995): one interface, a generic default, per-platform overrides
They are shaped like the store hierarchy, by the user's decision:
- `AbstractAsyncEventStore` holds the non-virtual public contract, checking arguments once, over protected `*Core` seams.
- `AsyncStoreEventStore` is a working default over **any** `IAsyncBulkStore<EventRecord>`.
- A backend whose native behaviour is better gets its own `Birko.Data.EventSourcing.<Backend>` project, which overrides
  the seams.

How the default works:
- **Concurrency without a backend index.** `EventRecord.Guid = EventRecord.IdFor(aggregate, version)` (RFC 9562 v5), so a
  second writer of one version creates an id that already exists, and every store refuses it. Measured on every database
  backend: `StoreUniqueViolationException` becomes `EventStoreConcurrencyException`.
- **The default appends one event at a time.** When a later event conflicts, it deletes the ones it wrote, then throws. A
  bulk create that meets a taken id leaves nothing, a prefix, or all but one, depending on the backend (measured), so only
  a sequential append knows what to undo. The transactional backends override the append.
- **A batch a crash cut short stays invisible, and is cleared later ([[TASK-1000]], the user's decisions).**
  - Every record of a batch of two or more carries `BatchGuid`, `BatchSize`, `BatchEnd` (the record id of its last
    event) and `WrittenAt`. A single event carries none: one write, as before (`BatchMarkingCostTests`).
  - Reads (`VisibleAsync`) show a batch only when `BatchSize` of its records are stored and none is an abort marker. A
    batch whose records are all in the page read costs nothing; another one is one lookup. `GetVersion` reads the top
    16 records and stops at the first visible one, skipping an incomplete batch above it.
  - An append that collides with an incomplete batch whose newest record is older than `AbandonedBatchLease` (30 s)
    clears it and retries once. It first creates an **abort marker** (`Aborted = true`) under `BatchEnd`: that create and
    the writer's own last create exclude each other, so a batch is either completed or cleared, never both. A batch with
    a marker is cleared at once, whatever the lease.
  - A failed batch is removed by `BatchGuid` (filter delete), never by record id: once a batch was cleared, its record
    ids can belong to another writer. After its last create a writer checks that its batch is whole, and fails
    (`EventStoreConcurrencyException`) rather than report a batch that was cleared under it.
  - `MakeVisibleAsync` (virtual, no-op) runs before those checks; Elasticsearch refreshes its index there, since the
    checks are searches.
  - The lease compares write times from the writers' clocks: clocks further apart than the lease can clear a live batch,
    whose writer then fails.
- **`factory.GetEventStore(o => o.AddSql().AddMongoDB()…)`** is an `IStoreFactory` extension. It answers a registered
  override that accepts the factory, otherwise the default over `factory.GetAsyncStore<EventRecord>()`.
  - Overrides are registered at the composition root, like backends: neither side can reference the other, and nothing
    is process-wide.
  - Two overrides that accept one factory are refused, by name.
  - JSON and XML are refused, because they are single-process only (measured).
- `FindConflictAsync` (protected) names the conflicting version, for overrides whose backend refuses a batch as a whole.

| Backend | Event store | A batch of events |
|---|---|---|
| SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server | `SqlEventStore<DB>` (Birko.Data.EventSourcing.SQL, `o.AddSql()`) | one transaction |
| MongoDB | `MongoDBEventStore` (Birko.Data.EventSourcing.MongoDB, `o.AddMongoDB()`) | one transaction on a replica set or sharded cluster; the default store on a standalone server |
| RavenDB | `RavenDBEventStore` (Birko.Data.EventSourcing.RavenDB, `o.AddRavenDB()`) | one session |
| Cosmos DB | `CosmosDBEventStore` (Birko.Data.EventSourcing.CosmosDB, `o.AddCosmosDB()`) | one transactional batch, one aggregate per batch |
| Elasticsearch | `ElasticSearchEventStore` (Birko.Data.EventSourcing.ElasticSearch, `o.AddElasticSearch()`) | the default store, plus an index refresh per append |
| InMemory (tests) | the default `AsyncStoreEventStore` | the default store |
| JSON, XML | refused: they cannot turn away a write from a second process | — |

The shared contract suite is `tests/Shared/EventSourcing/EventStoreContract.cs` (9 tests, including DraCode's two
writers). Every implementation's test project subclasses it. `tests/Shared/EventSourcing/CrashedBatchContract.cs`
(TASK-1000, 6 tests) runs on the backends that use the default append: InMemory, Elasticsearch and a standalone MongoDB.

`EventStoreConcurrencyException` (`AggregateGuid`, `Version`) is the contract's optimistic-concurrency signal: an append whose (aggregate, version) is already taken. A backend throws it and writes nothing from the batch.

### `IEventSourced` / `EventSourcedAggregate` (`Models/IEventSourced.cs`)
Entity contract for aggregates the wrappers can sit in front of:
- `long Version { get; set; }` — optimistic-concurrency token
- `ApplyEvent(IEvent)` — fold an event into the aggregate
- `GetUncommittedEvents()` / `MarkEventsAsCommitted()` — uncommitted-event buffer
- `LoadFromEvents(IEnumerable<IEvent>)` — replay helper

`EventSourcedAggregate` is a default base class that tracks uncommitted events in a `List<IEvent>`, sets `Version` from the applied event, and clears the buffer on commit.

### Wrappers (`Stores/`)
All four implement the same store interface as the inner store **and** `IStoreWrapper<T>`. Generic constraint: `T : AbstractModel, IEventSourced`. Constructor takes `(innerStore, eventStore, ISerializer? serializer = null, IDateTimeProvider? clock = null, Func<Guid?>? currentUser = null)`. Defaults: `SystemJsonSerializer`, `SystemDateTimeProvider`.

Write-side behavior is uniform across the four:
1. Compute `newVersion = eventStore.GetVersion(aggregateId) + 1`
2. Set `item.Version = newVersion`, then build a `DomainEvent("Created" | "Updated" | "Deleted", serializer.Serialize(item), currentUser?.Invoke(), clock)` (`NewEvent`, the one producer; TASK-713: the payload carried the old version)
3. **Append to event store first**, then delegate to the inner store

The bulk wrappers also implement the filter-based `Update(filter, PropertyUpdate<T>)`, `Update(filter, Action<T>)`, and `Delete(filter)` overloads — they read the matching entities, raise per-entity events via `AppendRange`, then call the inner bulk store. (No native UpdateByQuery / filter-delete optimization — event recording requires per-entity events.) A null filter, or one reducing to every row, is refused (TASK-713, `BoundedFilterGuard`; `x => true` is the explicit all-rows filter). A bulk update with an item without a Guid throws `EntityNotFoundException` before any event; a bulk delete leaves such items out.

Replay APIs (sync + async):
- `Replay(aggregateId)` — `CreateInstance()` + `IEventSourced.LoadFromEvents(events)`
- `GetHistory(aggregateId)` — raw event list for the aggregate

The optional `currentUser` delegate is read at each write and stamps `IEvent.UserGuid` (TASK-713: a settable `CurrentUserGuid` on a shared wrapper, now removed).

### `.WithEventSourcing(...)` extensions (`Stores/EventSourcingStoreExtensions.cs`)
One overload per store interface (`IStore<T>`, `IAsyncStore<T>`, `IBulkStore<T>`, `IAsyncBulkStore<T>`). Returns the same interface. The `IStore<T>` / `IAsyncStore<T>` overloads upcast to the bulk wrapper automatically if the store is already bulk.

## Usage

```csharp
public class Customer : AbstractModel, IEventSourced
{
    public long Version { get; set; }
    public string Name { get; set; } = string.Empty;

    // … implement ApplyEvent / GetUncommittedEvents / etc.
    // or inherit EventSourcedAggregate
}

IAsyncEventStore eventStore = /* your backend */;
IAsyncBulkStore<Customer> raw = new MongoStore<Customer>(/* … */);

var store = raw.WithEventSourcing(eventStore);   // returns IAsyncBulkStore<Customer>

await store.CreateAsync(new Customer { Name = "Acme" });
// → eventStore.AppendAsync(DomainEvent("Created", …)) then raw.CreateAsync(…)

var rebuilt = await ((AsyncEventSourcingBulkStoreWrapper<IAsyncBulkStore<Customer>, Customer>)store)
    .ReplayAsync(aggregateId);
```

To set the user on emitted events, pass `currentUser` (e.g. `() => auditContext.CurrentUserGuid`); `StoreWrapperBuilder` passes its `IAuditContext`'s.

## Composition
`Birko.Data.Composition.StoreWrapperBuilder.Build<T>` wires event sourcing into the decorator chain automatically — pass an `IAsyncEventStore` and any `T : IEventSourced` gets the wrapper applied innermost:

```csharp
var store = StoreWrapperBuilder.Build(raw, clock, audit, tenant, eventStore);
```

Chain order: `Tenant → Default → Sluggable → SoftDelete → Audit → Timestamp → EventSourcing → RawStore`. EventSourcing is innermost so the event payload reflects Timestamp/Audit enrichments and outer-wrapper rejections (slug collision, default conflict, tenant guard) do not produce orphan events. Soft-deletes emit an `"Updated"` event with `IsDeleted=true` because SoftDelete converts the delete before EventSourcing sees it.

To layer event sourcing manually (e.g. outside the builder, or to wrap an `IAsyncStore<T>` that isn't bulk), use the extension:

```csharp
var store = raw.WithEventSourcing(eventStore, clock);
```

## Dependencies
- Birko.Data.Core — `AbstractModel`, filters, `ModelByGuid<T>`
- Birko.Data.Stores — `IStore<T>`, `IAsyncStore<T>`, `IBulkStore<T>`, `IAsyncBulkStore<T>`, `IStoreWrapper<T>`, `StoreDataDelegate<T>`, `PropertyUpdate<T>`, `OrderBy<T>`
- Birko.Configuration
- Birko.Serialization — `ISerializer`; defaults to `SystemJsonSerializer` from `Birko.Serialization.Json`
- Birko.Time — `IDateTimeProvider`; defaults to `SystemDateTimeProvider`

## Conventions
- Concrete entities must implement `IEventSourced` (or extend `EventSourcedAggregate`).
- `EventType` is a string — only `"Created"` / `"Updated"` / `"Deleted"` are emitted by the wrappers. Custom event types require a custom path (raise via `eventStore.Append` directly, or subclass a wrapper).
- Events are appended **before** the inner write — if the inner write fails, you may end up with an event for a row that doesn't exist. Atomicity is the responsibility of the event-store backend (transaction with the inner store, outbox, etc.).
- Bulk filter-based `Update(filter, …)` / `Delete(filter)` are read-modify-write internally so that per-aggregate events can be emitted. Do not expect native UpdateByQuery performance.

## Not Included (Plan If Needed)
- A sync `IEventStore` implementation: only the async contract is implemented (TASK-995).
- Snapshot store — not modeled here despite earlier docs mentioning it.
- Projections / read-model fan-out — see `Birko.EventBus.EventSourcing` for replay/event-bus glue (`DomainEventPublished`, `EventReplayService`, `EventStoreEventBus`).
